The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Parade That Came in Backward

Daisy took a turn pulling a little cart of seed buns toward the birdhouse. Toad marched behind with a flag. Bella marched behind Toad with a smaller flag. They were trying out an Everybody Day parade.

The lane ended at a stump. Daisy could have flown over it. Toad could have hopped. The seed buns, despite all the exciting things going on, had never learned to fly.

“Turn around!” Daisy called. Toad turned. Bella turned. Daisy turned. The cart stayed exactly where it was. Then everybody bumped into the buns. The one on top acquired a neat toad-shaped dent.

Bella could see daylight behind her. “Would you like to come this way?” she called. She lowered her little flag backward. Toad followed the flag. Daisy walked the cart backward one wheel turn at a time.

They came out beside the stump in a broad grassy ring. Bella marched around it. Toad marched around it. The cart followed in a lovely sweeping curve. Nothing bumped anything, except the flag bumping Bella’s bottom.

At the gate Daisy checked the ring with the cart going both ways. “We can show the whole loop,” she said. “Somebody with wheels may want to know how to get back out.”

Daisy drew a loop around a stump on a leaf for the Welcome Tree. At the gate she put up a copy. “Who’s going to lead the real parade?” asked Toad. Daisy looked at the small flag.

On the way home Bella marched in front. Daisy marched in back. At the birdhouse they shared the seed buns. Toad asked for the dented one. “I believe,” he said, “we have met before.”

Read together

How would you lead a parade if the last walker could hear you best?
